messages:
marta: noticed a handful of clients (mobile SDK v1.2.x) still sending the old binary-chunk framing (2-byte length prefix) instead of our current 4-byte little-endian framing. causes stream parse errors on the fast-path and spikes p95 timeouts.

derek: numbers? is this concentrated?

marta: about 0.4% of streaming sessions last 48h, mostly older mobile app builds + one small integration partner. metric: legacy_frame.incr (tagged by tenant).

kai: we promised no hard breaks for streaming. options: a) runtime-side converter that upgrades 2-byte -> 4-byte on the fly, b) sidecar proxy for affected tenants, c) extended client-deprecation with opt-in header.

nora: converter seems simplest operationally. but watch out for perf and memory safety on the hot path. converting every stream chunk could increase allocations.

marta: proposed approach: detect legacy framing at session start (inspect first 2-4 bytes), set a per-connection mode. Only run conversion for connections flagged legacy. Conversion rules: read 2-byte BE length, rewrite to 4-byte LE length, keep chunk payload unchanged. If chunk size > 64KB -> reject (legacy_frame.reject.size).

derek: also add a fast-path failure: if a connection toggles between legacy and modern frames mid-session, close with 400 and emit legacy_frame.mixed. simpler than trying to be magic.

kai: implementation notes for runtime: small C++ shim in the streaming ingress reader. Use a reusable buffer (preallocated) for rewrite to avoid frequent heap allocs. Instrument with histograms for convert latency.

marta: rollout plan: default OFF for all new tenants; enable per-tenant via console toggle `compat.streaming_frame_converter`. Hosted can enable for affected tenants; Dedicated/Private exposed as config flag for ops.

nora: security: ensure converter runs before authentication is validated? we should do framing detection+convert first so auth parsers get the expected payload, then run auth. but log if auth-after-convert fails (legacy_frame.auth_fail) to catch weird clients.

derek: telemetry: emit legacy_frame.detect, legacy_frame.converted, legacy_frame.rejected, legacy_frame.mixed. Add tenant_id tags. Also surface top callers in console to drive outreach.

marta: cost/billing: small CPU/memory; attach billing tag `compat.streaming_convert_cpu` when enabled so tenants see marginal cost. ops agreed.

kai: guardrails: 1) rate-limit conversion throughput per-tenant (default 1000/s) 2) circuit-breaker: if converted p50 latency +8ms or error-rate delta >0.3% in a 5m window, auto-disable for that tenant. 3) safety net: conversion respects max chunk limit and total message size limit (2MB).

nora: tests: unit tests for BE->LE rewrite, fuzz malformed prefixes, e2e with partial frames, integration test with TLS + streaming load. we should also run long-lived session test to ensure no memory leaks.

deploy-bot: staging deploy queued for branch: feature/stream-frame-converter (sha: c3f9a7d)

derek: docs/outreach: notify the integration partner and the two mobile teams with example patches to switch to 4-byte framing. provide a snippet: 
```
// client patch: write 4-byte LE length
uint32_t len = payload.size();
write_le32(stream, len);
stream.write(payload);
```

marta: lifecycle: keep converter supported for 4 months after GA, then announce removal window of 90 days. show these dates in console.

kai: follow-up work: microbench numbers (allocs and p99 added), sandbox the static buffer pool, and add an opt-in env var for local testing.

ops-bot: alert created for tenant "acme-mobile" to track legacy_frame.incr spikes.

derek: I'll file the RFC follow-up with design doc, perf graphs, and rollout playbook. assign to @kai + @nora for review.

marta: +1 from runtime and product. security ok with auth-after-convert logging.

kai: +1, will attach perf PR.

derek: action items:
- derek: RFC + rollout playbook + tenant outreach draft
- kai: perf microbench + buffer pool prototype
- nora: test matrix + security review checklist
- marta: implement runtime shim and staging CI

marta: thanks all. if no objections we'll start canary next week on the small partner tenant.

derek: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/rfcs/pulls/499 — PTAL and give thumbs.
